sampling_model.design: The data are dominated and i.i.d. on the canonical full ball \(\mathcal V_P=\{P':\|dP'/dP-1\|_\infty<\varepsilon\}\), intersected with the full transported fixed-nullity, fixed-cokernel, reduced-modulus-separated stratum and both bridge-solvability loci. Every DQM curve remaining in that intersection is admissible; tangent richness is not part of the model definition.
sampling_model.units: The sampling units are \(O_i=(Y_i,A_i,Z_i,W_i,X_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), independently distributed according to \(P\).
sampling_model.treatment: The treatment \(A\) is binary. The statistical target is the observed joint-bridge functional; its equality with the ATE uses the separately stated latent consistency, exchangeability, positivity, negative-control, and bridge-compatibility conditions.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment-bridge existence is an observed solvability restriction. The main model imposes no injectivity, surjectivity, preferred minimum-norm bridge, or bridge uniqueness.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For each evaluation fold, its complement is split into construction and calibration samples of order \(n\). All bridge representatives and dictionary functions are learned only on the construction sample; the fixed learned dictionary is evaluated on the independent calibration sample to form a thresholded-and-ridged Gram projection; the resulting affine signal is evaluated only on the held-out fold. The conditions expose fourth-norm multipliers, square-root dimension aggregation, calibration exponential-moment rates, positive-eigenvalue and cutoff separation, coefficient and weight envelopes, sieve approximation, and the primal--dual mixed-bias product.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The public manuscript supplies selected-pair inverse-problem inference architecture; the final publisher theorem scope remains unverified, and no publisher-only claim is used.

The paper motivates outcome-only overidentification, but its exact model and parameter were not imported; the proved comparison instead uses an explicit fixed-rank selected parameter.
Theorem \(3.1\) is the unique-and-surjective endpoint motivating the bijective sanity check.
Increasing-moment GMM informs implementation but does not establish the present independent-calibration, singular-Gram affine projection bound.
The unique-bridge data-combination result concerns a different statistical model.

Quotient-functional efficiency is prior art; the unresolved novelty is the coupled proximal tangent-lifting theorem, while the nested attaining projection is proved conditionally on that geometry and explicit estimator rates.

body.tldr: The unrestricted score-lifting equality remains open: continuous moving kernels do not supply the coupled local parameterization required to realize every annihilator direction. The general efficiency result is therefore repaired to a proved one-way theorem: tangent equality plus one square-integrable bridge score and an explicit pathwise primal--dual product remainder yield the affine-quotient canonical gradient. The estimator is repaired by nested construction/calibration/evaluation splitting and calibration spectral cutoff. Under dimension-aware multiplier, concentration, cutoff, coefficient, approximation, and mixed-bias conditions it has pointwise asymptotic linearity, ratio-consistent variance, and Wald coverage; regularity is proved only for contiguous path classes satisfying the displayed uniform versions of every condition. The exact finite efficiency and nonattainment witnesses remain unchanged, and the observed bridge functional is a causal ATE only under the separate identification proposition.

project_justification.gap: Existing nonunique-bridge inference results do not identify the full tangent closure of the simultaneous outcome- and treatment-solvability germ. The remaining geometric gap is actual path realization on the unrestricted fixed-defect Hilbert stratum; pathwise differentiability alone also does not presently force an individual square-integrable bridge score.
project_justification.niche: The contribution isolates quotient-tangent efficiency with two nonunique bridge fibers and supplies a variance-minimizing affine estimator whose construction remains valid for singular population Grams through an independent calibration split and spectral cutoff.
project_justification.fill: The proved general results are the exact mixed-bias sufficient theorem, the affine Hilbert projection conditional on tangent equality, the dimension-aware nested calibration projection bound, pointwise efficient inference under explicit rates, and a locally uniform extension under fully quantified contiguous-path conditions. Reverse score lifting and the bridge-score necessity direction remain open; exact finite germs supply unconditional positive witnesses.

body.related_work: Bennett et al. provide the exact proximal mixed-bias architecture and product-rate logic, while Zhang et al. emphasize bridge nonuniqueness; neither is used to assert the unresolved tangent equality on this two-fiber saturated germ. Imbens et al., Ai--Shan, and uniqueness/surjectivity-restricted proximal efficiency results do not establish the quotient result here. Ai--Chen motivates Galerkin regularization, but the independent calibration layer, singular-Gram spectral cutoff, and affine coefficient accounting are explicit additional repairs. Chen--Santos identifies which local-product attainability and bounded-direction density facts would be needed for reverse lifting; those hypotheses have been audited and are not consequences of operator continuity. No claim relies on unverified publisher-only wording.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The coupled score-lifting kernel is unresolved in the unrestricted Hilbert model. The frozen chart supplies continuous, not differentiable, moving kernel and cokernel projections and no locally onto parameterization of the joint solvability incidence set with a shared \((W,X)\) marginal. The proved estimator theorem is conditional on explicit construction, calibration, spectral, approximation, and mixed-bias rates; its regularity conclusion additionally requires their uniform versions, \(L^2\) continuity and uniform integrability of the canonical gradient, a uniform target expansion, LAN, and Lindeberg. Compact-operator closed-range collapse and rank-changing neighborhoods remain outside scope.
body.honest_scope: Unconditional claims remain the algebraic normal--affine identity, operator-kernel stability, and the certified finite tangent and nonattainment witnesses. In the general model, tangent equality is an unresolved premise. Conditional on that equality and the displayed nearby-bridge product condition, the affine projection is the canonical gradient. The repaired nested estimator attains pointwise Gaussian inference under explicit rates, and is regular and locally efficient only on contiguous path classes satisfying every displayed uniform condition. No iff between pathwise differentiability and bridge-score existence, no unqualified global efficiency, and no automatic causal interpretation are claimed.
body.interpretation: With redundant proxies, a chosen bridge pair can have a valid pathwise score under the displayed product condition without minimizing variance over the affine score hull. When tangent equality is available, the nested affine projection supplies the variance-minimizing replacement and valid pointwise Wald inference under the corrected rates. For SUPPORT, bridge-dependent standard errors can therefore be compared with this affine replacement, but global efficiency on the unrestricted observed-law germ still requires score lifting, and causal interpretation still requires the separate latent identification conditions.
